decision: Three additive migrations — 019_role.sql, 020_role_assignment.sql, 021_grant_role_fk.sql — plus two known_tenant_tables.txt lines and updates to the two affected DB-fitness test files (schema.test.ts FF-FK-RESOLVE, cross_tenant.test.ts seed dispatcher). role and role_assignment are plain T-0013 tenant tables (tenant_id leading PK, FORCE RLS, default-DENY, choros_app DML). org_scope is jsonb NOT NULL carrying the EXISTING grant-lattice.ts org-ScopeElement shape (node or set, hierarchy=org, nodeLevel in {department,position}) — no new scope algebra, no DB structural CHECK (mirrors grant.scope jsonb). Validity window valid_from/until bigint NULL, half-open, no from<until CHECK. proposed_by/confirmed_by text NULL with confirmed_by IS NULL => proposal (zero grants) / NOT NULL => confirmed, realized at the resolution boundary not a DB CHECK. Migration 021 promotes grant.role_id to a named tenant-scoped FK grant_role_id_fkey -> role(tenant_id,id) (pure additive ALTER; verified safe — grant table is empty in dev base). The role->grant resolution chain is fixed as a CONTRACT consumed by T-0053; src/core/grant-resolver.ts and grant-lattice.ts are NOT edited (NF-6/AC-20, enforced by grant-resolver-isolation.sh). All DB-level ACs were validated live against an isolated Postgres (001-016+019-021 applied, idempotent re-run, full negative-path + cross-tenant probes under real choros_app).

rejected_alternatives.option: A new org-scope algebra / separate scope_dept_id+scope_pos_id columns
rejected_alternatives.why_not: NF-3 violation — second scope grammar. grant-lattice.ts org-ScopeElement already encodes node-or-set over the org hierarchy with working AncestryOracle containment; reusing it as jsonb keeps ONE scope model that T-0029 reads.

rejected_alternatives.option: Normalized link table role_assignment_scope(assignment_id, node_id, node_level) for the SET
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Over-engineering (rubric ax.5). The set is small, read whole by the resolver, and the lattice consumes a single serialized ScopeElement; grant.scope jsonb set the precedent for scope-sets-as-jsonb.

rejected_alternatives.option: DB CHECK that org_scope is well-formed (hierarchy=org, nodeId resolves)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Inconsistent with grant.scope jsonb (no structural CHECK). nodeId existence is a cross-table predicate not expressible as a column CHECK; write-API is the validation seam. DB enforces NOT NULL + valid jsonb (the type does that).
AC-10 explicitly forbids it — window sanity is application-layer, matching grant. A confirmed-but-expired window is a legitimate stored state the resolver filters at read time.

rejected_alternatives.option: Fold the FK into 020 or back-patch 008 instead of a separate 021
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Splitting keeps each migration independently appliable and the FK a pure additive ALTER after role exists; back-patching 008 would rewrite frozen history and break the recorded schema_migrations version.
FR-2 — same role in different subtree/window is a real case; de-dup is application-layer, consistent with grant having no such constraint.

rejected_alternatives.option: Edit grant-resolver.ts to wire role->grant now
rejected_alternatives.why_not: NF-6/AC-20 — T-0033 edits the resolver in parallel (write-conflict); DB-backed getGrants is T-0053 per the T-0021 ADR. T-0022 ships the column contract only.

rejected_alternatives.option: A person_grant / agent_role fork for human vs agent subjects
rejected_alternatives.why_not: AC-22 — roles are ONE table; both employee kinds bind through the single role_assignment (employee.id is kind-agnostic, the org tables already unified human/agent in one employee table).

contracts: PK both tables: (tenant_id, id). UNIQUE(tenant_id, slug) on role only. No UNIQUE(employee_id, role_id) on role_assignment.
RLS both tables: ENABLE+FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; policy USING/WITH CHECK tenant_id=current_setting('choros.tenant_id',true)::uuid; GRANT SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE TO choros_app.

T-0053 resolution contract (interface point, grant-resolver.ts NOT edited): effective grants = grants attached via grant.role_id to roles for which subject has a role_assignment that is (a) confirmed (confirmed_by IS NOT NULL), (b) in-window (isEffective half-open over valid_from/valid_until), (c) whose org_scope admits the org context via the EXISTING AncestryOracle. Proposal => 0 grants; out-of-window => 0 grants.

C-1 COMPAT (FE-W23-0008): ci/checks/db/schema.test.ts FF-FK-RESOLVE breaks post-021 — 'grant.role_id carries no FK' inverts and not.toContain('role') inverts. coder MUST update it to a positive grant_role_id_fkey->role assertion, admit role/role_assignment as valid FK targets, and extend the FK-pairs arrayContaining (role_assignment->employee, role_assignment->role, grant->role). This file is in ci/checks/db/, NOT in the AC-20 frozen src/core/ set.

C-2 COMPAT (FE-W23-0008): ci/checks/db/cross_tenant.test.ts seedRowForTable dispatcher default-throws 'unknown table' — adding role/role_assignment to the fixture makes the generic KNOWN_TENANT_TABLES iteration throw. coder MUST add case 'role' and case 'role_assignment' to the dispatcher + seedState (role after tenant; role_assignment after employee+role). cross-tenant-fitness.sh tokens (KNOWN_TENANT_TABLES/appUrl/migratorUrl) stay satisfied.

No other KNOWN_TENANT_TABLES consumer breaks: two_tenant.test.ts does not iterate the list; object-handle.test.ts uses a local constant; pgTimerStore references it only in a comment (verified by grep over all consumers).
Seed-ordering invariant for downstream: any future grant seed MUST reference a role seeded in 019 (019 role precedes any grant data; grant table is empty today so 021 FK validation finds no orphan).

T-0029 reads role_assignment.org_scope as the non-widenable lattice-shaped admin boundary; T-0039 owns proposed_by/confirmed_by workflow + source='llm-proposed'; T-0019 references role.id point-in-time (NOT a live FK, role.id never re-keyed); T-0032 evaluates SoD over confirmed in-window role_assignment rows.
